title: Quantitative multivariate local central limit theorem for irreducible measures on the discrete cube
author: Pietro Caputo; Daniel Parisi
work: Nonlinear recombinations and generalized random transpositions
difficulty_reason: The claim is a lattice local CLT for mu^{otimes N} on {0,...,N}^K with error C/N^{(K+1)/2} that is uniform over the maximum in M_N, so the proof must compare an exact point mass with a Gaussian density rather than a distribution function. The complete proof at 2289-2325 splits the Fourier difference into three pieces - the Gaussian comparison on A_N = {|s| <= 1/(4L_N)}, the far region Q_{N,K} minus A_N killed by the exponential characteristic-function bound |psi(t)| <= exp(-c<t,t>) coming from irreducibility, and the Gaussian tail on the complement of A_N - each shown to be O(1/sqrt(N)) before the prefactor B_N^{-1} = N^{-K/2}(det V_1)^{-1/2}. The first piece is not free: it needs the uniform comparison |phi_N(t) - exp(-<t,t>/2)| <= 16 L_N|t|^3 exp(-<t,t>/3) for |t| <= 1/(4L_N), whose proof at 2213-2286 is a two-regime argument that restarts at |t| < (1/2)L_N^{-1/3} because the cubic Taylor remainder is not small there.

primary.label: Proposition prop:LCLT: lattice local CLT with error C/N^{(K+1)/2}, uniform over the maximum in M_N
